quotes.text: Relationship intelligence is like someone opening that file and asking, are we still talking to these people?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A plain-language analogy for what the feature does.

quotes.text: The tool can organize communication signals, but it cannot fill in conversations that were never captured. That's just how it works.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reminds that the insights depend on activity being recorded.

quotes.text: A single score gives you a snapshot. The trend shows whether the relationship is gaining attention, losing attention, or staying flat while the deal moves through its stages.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why to watch the health trend rather than one label.

quotes.text: Relationship health tells you where to look. It can't replace the conversation that brings a customer back into the deal.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear statement that signals guide, but do not replace, selling.

quotes.text: Don't treat a colleague's past contact as permission to use their relationship. Send a short note, explain who you want to meet and why.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical etiquette for using warm introductions.

takeaways: Relationship intelligence in Dynamics 365 Sales turns emails, meetings and calls tied to sales records into signals that show whether a customer is still engaged.
Basic insights update close to real time from Dynamics 365 activities, while enhanced insights add Exchange data via server-side synchronization and refresh every 24 hours.

Relationship health and who knows whom point sellers to the relationships that need attention and to colleagues for warm introductions, but the seller still has to judge the context and have the conversation.
hook: A Dynamics 365 Sales opportunity can look busy while the customer has quietly stopped replying. This episode explains relationship intelligence for sellers, sales managers and CRM admins: relationship analytics, relationship health and who knows whom, and how to turn those signals into the next useful customer conversation.
